A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Object-X with the same authors, research objectives and core pipeline. The text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, localization and scene-alignment experiments on 3RScan and ScanNet, plus compression, occlusion and auxiliary-modality ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative and qualitative single-image reconstruction comparisons with MIDI.

M1.justification: The architecture is retained, but Section 3.2 changes the stated compression objective from averaging over L active voxels to all N^3 grid cells. Section 3.4 specifies task loss alone during frozen-core training, retaining the combined objective for joint fine-tuning. These are limited objective-specification revisions; changed implementation or training runs are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use 3RScan and ScanNet with the same reconstruction, localization, alignment and occlusion scenarios. The new MIDI comparison uses a subset of the already evaluated 3RScan single-image task, without adding a dataset, domain or input requirement.

E2.justification: v2 adds MIDI as an evaluated single-image reconstruction comparator in Table 2 and Figure 9. The existing 3DGS, 2DGS, DepthSplat, SceneGraphLoc, CrossOver, SGAligner and EVA comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 2 introduces a separate 3RScan-subset evaluation reporting accuracy, completion and F1 at 5 cm, beyond the existing single-image photometric/F1 comparison. Original splits, view selection and optimization budgets remain unchanged. The new subset size, selection and registration procedure are unclear; the caption references asterisks absent from the rows.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Figure 9 add four qualitative cases examining MIDI's geometric mismatches against ground truth and Object-X reconstructions. The existing latent-resolution, occlusion and localization ablations are retained; v1 Appendix E becomes v2 Appendix F.

E5.justification: The compression and occlusion tables retain identical mean ± sigma and median reporting. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. The new checklist comments on statistical reporting without changing the analyses.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds F1@0.05 results of 34.516 for MIDI, 48.397 for Object-X RGB and 63.223 for Object-X RGB-D, alongside accuracy and completion scores. Figure 9 adds qualitative findings. Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged; the new subset scores do not establish improvements over v1's evaluation.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the compression-loss summation limit and normalization from L to N^3, making the formal definition cover the full grid with occupied/unoccupied weighting. No theorem or proof is added. Renaming the Gaussian count from N to M is only notational.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: reconstructable multimodal object embeddings, competitive downstream performance and storage reductions of 3–4 orders of magnitude. The additional MIDI evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly attributes geometric accuracy to voxel-grounded surface constraints and interprets MIDI's errors through domain shift and generative versus reconstructive modeling. The conclusion also states more definitely that zero-shot performance does not consistently match optimized task-specific methods.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly directs readers to the code for scenes used in the MIDI comparison, and the checklist adds submission-time release disclosures. Existing hardware, learning rates, iteration counts, preprocessing details and repository URL are retained. The PDFs do not establish an actual change in external resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds MIDI and distinguishes its generative objective from Object-X's metrically grounded reconstruction. It also adds Depth Anything V2, StableNormal and VGGT as potential sources of future geometric priors. The existing related-work survey and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify compression, auxiliary training, baseline fairness and result interpretation, alongside typo corrections. v2 adds acknowledgements, a NeurIPS checklist and a short single-image appendix while preserving the scientific narrative and most existing text.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MIDI comparison table and Figure 9, redraws Figure 1, and refines and enlarges Figure 2 with clearer latent labels. Existing displays are resized or relocated, while most original tables and qualitative panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected loss definition and clearer diagrams improve interpretability, while MIDI provides a relevant generative comparator beyond v1's single-image 3DGS comparison. These gains are limited: the new experiment leaves subset and registration details unclear, and Object-X's training on 3RScan weakens the broader domain-shift interpretation. The original core results remain intact.
